A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RainPro-8 research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, architecture diagrams and forecast visualizations, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original European forecasting experiments, ablations, input-attribution analyses and forecast examples in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original European results and adds RainPro-2R results on SEVIR and a three-run comparison of loss variants. Table 3 distinguishes borrowed comparator scores from the work's own results.

M1.justification: Appendix H introduces the RainPro-2R adaptation with radar-only inputs, no additional spatial context and twenty output frames. This is a limited input/output adaptation: the principal RainPro-8 architecture, ordinal masked loss, lead-time weighting and single-pass procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds SEVIR storm-event nowcasting, predicting twenty frames from five radar frames, alongside the retained European eight-hour forecasting task. This substantially extends evaluation to different data, a shorter prediction horizon and an input setting without additional spatial context.

E2.justification: NowcastNet disappears from the European comparisons, while RainPro-8R enters the main comparison and corresponding appendix results. The new SEVIR comparison adds PhyDnet, MAU, ConvGRU, STRPM, MCVD, PreDiff and DiffCast; its comparator scores in Table 3 are explicitly attributed to DiffCast rather than presented as newly rerun baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix H adds a SEVIR protocol using 128×128 frames, 200K Adam iterations, learning rate 0.0001, lead-time decay 2, and additional pooled and perceptual metrics. The European setup is largely retained. Table 2 changes the CE ablation's lead-time weighting entry from '-' to enabled despite identical scores; this establishes a reported-setting revision, not a rerun.

E4.justification: v2 removes the separate OC-mask ablation and revises the source-control presentation to explicit radar-only RainPro-8R. Appendix G adds a targeted analysis of initialization variability for ordinal versus cross-entropy loss. The other principal ablations, Integrated Gradients analyses and selected European case studies remain.

E5.justification: Unlike v1, Appendix G reports means and standard deviations across three independent runs for RainPro-8 and its CE variant over six metrics. It also newly discloses that the primary experiments used single training runs. This introduces statistical context for the small loss-function differences, without establishing v1's run counts or adding significance tests.

E6.justification: Retained European headline scores are unchanged, but NowcastNet and no-mask results disappear. The source-control CSI changes from 0.2538 to 0.2289 under the explicit radar-only label; exact input-setting equivalence is unresolved. New SEVIR results include CSI 0.3524 versus DiffCast's 0.3077, but CSI-p16 0.4171 versus 0.5683. Figures and appendices also add CRPS/FSS comparisons, inference timings and three-run aggregates.

T1.justification: The probability factorization, monotonicity argument and lead-time weighting mathematics are retained. Equation 6 restates the existing masked average using an eligible-index set. Appendix H's standard HSS formula supplies metric documentation rather than new theory or a substantive derivation.

C1.justification: v1's contributions center on efficient eight-hour European forecasting. v2 adds versatility in short-term radar-only forecasting and state-of-the-art SEVIR performance against deterministic and generative models as an explicit main contribution. The original efficiency, ordinal consistency and operational-comparison claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations separating input-source benefits from model benefits and discussing SEVIR's pixel-accuracy versus pooled/perceptual-quality tradeoff. It removes the explanation for the no-mask ablation and future-work suggestions concerning structural input changes and alternatives to GFS. Missing-input robustness remains future work.

D1.justification: Existing European preprocessing, hyperparameters and hardware disclosures are retained. v2 adds SEVIR implementation settings, per-sample inference times and a reproducibility statement promising code and data-access instructions. The abstract still contains an unfilled 'URL', so the PDFs do not establish an accessible code release.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused references and positioning for SEVIR, DiffCast, additional short-term comparators and perceptual metrics. The broader discussion of MetNet, numerical forecasting, extrapolation and medium-range models remains substantially the same.

P1.justification: The introduction, method explanations and experimental discussion undergo extensive condensation and rewriting, with clearer descriptive ablation names. v2 adds a SEVIR subsection and reproducibility statement, and reorganizes appendices around compute resources, robustness and SEVIR while relocating the GFS variable list.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template, title treatment, headings, running headers, spacing and figure placement. It adds the SEVIR table and comparison figure, a variability table and an inference-time column; removes the OC-mask column; and replaces NowcastNet curves and forecast panels with RainPro-8R. Existing attribution and probability-map displays are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The SEVIR evaluation and expanded European radar-only comparison strengthen evidence beyond v1's single-dataset evaluation, while Appendix G makes the small loss-function advantages easier to assess. Inference timings also better document efficiency. These benefits outweigh the loss of NowcastNet and the separate mask ablation, but limited repeated-run coverage, unresolved source-control comparability and placeholder code access constrain the overall improvement.
